requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.invocation` has no implementation edges and no review roots. Every clause specifies observable CLI behavior, not how the code is built.

- The command form `habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]` is the user-facing syntax. Any argument parser or declaration that accepts the same arguments behaves identically, so this is not a structural obligation.
- The clause "MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example" describes which subject is chosen. Selection could use a different lookup mechanism with the same result. Behavior after the first assessment is delegated by citation to `requirements.authoring.refresh` and `requirements.authoring.reassessment`. Those cited texts supply context only.
- The completion report must name the subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage-record path. The destination must be the evidence-file path by default or stdout under `--stdout`. In stdout mode the report and diagnostics must go to stderr. These are all output contents and stream choices, so they are observable.
- "`author-evidence` MUST remain an alias" means the old name behaves the same as the new one. It does not matter whether it is a clap alias, a separate subcommand that delegates, or something else. The behavior is the same.

No clause names a required library, algorithm, type, field, signature or delegation through a named interface. No implementation roots are needed.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.authoring.invocation`.

- **Subject selection.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs `author` on an existing requirement and on an existing named example. Both runs succeed and write evidence under `evidence/<subject>.json`. `fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` shows that an absent name, `requirements.absent`, is rejected with the name in stderr and that existing evidence is left unchanged.
- **Initial selection and later assessments.** These are governed by the cited `requirements.authoring.refresh` and `requirements.authoring.reassessment`. They are not reassessed here. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` also carries a `{test}` marker for this requirement. It exercises the `--missing`, `--force` and `--stdout` forms of the command line.
- **Completion report.** `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`. It asserts an `Evidence:` line whose path is the project's `evidence/SUBJECT.json`, and a `Usage:` line. The initial-prompt test asserts the subject, backend and model line, the evidence path, and that the usage path names an existing file.
- **Evidence destination.** By default it is the evidence-file path, as asserted above. With `--stdout`, `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts `Evidence: stdout\n` on stderr. It also checks that the evidence file is unchanged and that no `evidence` directory is created when none existed.
- **Stdout mode streams.** The same test parses stdout as the evidence JSON only. The report line (subject, backend, model), the `Usage:` path and the verbose false rationale appear on stderr. `fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` shows that with `--stdout`, failures leave stdout empty and stderr carries the diagnostics, such as the "even after a reminder" message.
- **Alias.** `author-evidence` is used in the stdout test, the failure test, the batch test and the conflict test. The `--stdout` runs, the failure runs and the batch runs show it behaves as the single-subject command.
- **Command-line options.** `--config` is tested in `fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]`. It asserts the non-default profile's model, key and backend are used. `-v` and `--verbose` are tested in `fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]`. `--missing` and `--force` are tested in the batch test, including the conflict rejection. The conflict test in `fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` shows a subject name and `--all` are rejected together.

The assertions check the stated outcomes, and I found no unaddressed obligation or plausible violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST initially assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current on initial selection.
After that selection, {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment` governs each round. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
:::{req} reassessment
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.
A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
